items.stem: What is the source document for an entry in the sales returns journal?
options: A credit note received from a supplier
An invoice sent to the customer
A credit note sent to the customer
items.answer: A credit note sent to the customer
items.markingKey: A credit note sent to the customer. Returns inwards are recorded from copies of credit notes issued [1]

items.stem: Explain the difference between trade discount and cash discount.
items.answer: Trade discount is a reduction in list price given to trade customers, usually for bulk buying, and is not recorded in the accounts; cash discount is an allowance for prompt payment, recorded as discount allowed/received.
items.markingKey: Trade discount – reduction in list price, not recorded [1]; cash discount – prompt payment, recorded [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain two advantages of using books of prime entry instead of posting every transaction directly to the ledger.
items.answer: Transactions of the same type are listed together so only totals are posted to the general ledger, reducing work and errors; they provide a chronological record and make it easier to divide the work among staff.
items.markingKey: Fewer postings/totals only [1]; reduce errors or division of work or chronological record [1] [2]

items.stem: The following credit transactions of Lotus Retail took place in July: sold goods on credit to Daniel, list price $1,700, no trade discount; sold goods on credit to Jonas, list price $3,400, less 20% trade discount; sold goods on credit to Nadia, list price $3,000, less 10% trade discount; sold goods on credit to Mateo, list price $3,200, less 20% trade discount. (a) Calculate the amount entered in the sales journal for each transaction and the total of the journal. (b) Explain why trade discount is not recorded in the ledger accounts of Lotus Retail.
items.answer: (a) Daniel $1,700; Jonas $2,720; Nadia $2,700; Mateo $2,560; total $9,680 (b) Trade discount is a reduction in the list price given to trade customers before the invoice is issued; it is not a separate transaction, so only the net invoice value is recorded.
items.markingKey: (a) Daniel $1,700 × 100% = $1,700; Jonas $3,400 × 80% = $2,720; Nadia $3,000 × 90% = $2,700; Mateo $3,200 × 80% = $2,560 [3]; total $9,680 [1] [4] (b) Reduction from list price at the time of sale [1]; only net invoice value recorded [1] [2]

items.stem: State the double entry made when the sales returns journal total is posted.
items.answer: Debit the sales returns account with the total; credit each customer's account in the sales ledger with the individual amounts.

items.stem: Explain why the discount columns in a three-column cash book are memorandum columns.
items.answer: They are not part of the double entry in the cash book; their totals are posted to the discount allowed and discount received accounts in the general ledger.
items.markingKey: Not part of cash/bank double entry [1]; totals posted to discount accounts in general ledger [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business offers cash discount to its credit customers.
items.answer: To encourage customers to pay early, improving cash flow and reducing the risk of irrecoverable debts.
items.markingKey: Encourage prompt payment [1]; improves liquidity/reduces bad debts [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the cash column of a cash book can never have a credit balance.
items.answer: A business cannot pay out more cash than it holds, so total cash payments can never exceed cash receipts plus the opening balance.

items.stem: Which document supports each payment in the petty cash book?
items.answer: A petty cash voucher
items.markingKey: A petty cash voucher. Vouchers are signed and authorised for each payment [1]

items.stem: Explain two advantages of the imprest system of petty cash.
items.answer: The cashier can only spend the float, so overspending and fraud are limited and cash can be checked at any time (cash + vouchers = imprest); the main cashier is not troubled with small payments.
items.markingKey: Control – cash + vouchers = imprest, limits fraud [1]; saves the main cashier's time/delegation [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the general journal is used for the purchase of non-current assets on credit.
items.answer: No other book of prime entry deals with it (the purchases journal is only for goods for resale), and the journal provides a record and explanation of an infrequent, high-value transaction.
items.markingKey: Not goods for resale – no other book [1]; record/narrative for unusual item [1] [2]

items.stem: State two uses of the general journal.
items.answer: Opening entries; purchase/sale of non-current assets on credit; correction of errors; writing off irrecoverable debts; year-end transfers.
items.markingKey: Any two [1 each] [2]

items.stem: The following credit transactions of Coral Bay Foods took place in July: sold goods on credit to Tomás, list price $1,700, less 20% trade discount; sold goods on credit to Nadia, list price $4,400, no trade discount. A trainee accountant entered a total of $6,100 in the sales journal. State the mistake made and give the correct journal total.
items.answer: The list prices were recorded without deducting trade discount; only the net invoice value is recorded. Correct journal total: $5,760.
items.markingKey: Error: the list prices were recorded without deducting trade discount; only the net invoice value is recorded [1]; correct journal total: $5,760 [1] [2]

items.stem: The following credit transactions of Monsoon Garments took place in July: sold goods on credit to Leila, list price $2,300, less 20% trade discount; sold goods on credit to Sipho, list price $1,800, no trade discount. Calculate the amount entered in the sales journal for each transaction and the total of the journal.
items.answer: Leila $1,840; Sipho $1,800; total $3,640

items.stem: The following credit transactions of Baobab Furnishings took place in July: bought goods on credit from Mateo, list price $800, less 10% trade discount; bought goods on credit from Amara, list price $5,900, less 25% trade discount; bought goods on credit from Ines, list price $1,100, less 15% trade discount; bought goods on credit from Leila, list price $4,400, less 10% trade discount. (a) Calculate the amount entered in the purchases journal for each transaction and the total of the journal. (b) Explain why trade discount is not recorded in the ledger accounts of Baobab Furnishings.
items.answer: (a) Mateo $720; Amara $4,425; Ines $935; Leila $3,960; total $10,040 (b) Trade discount is a reduction in the list price given to trade customers before the invoice is issued; it is not a separate transaction, so only the net invoice value is recorded.
items.markingKey: (a) Mateo $800 × 90% = $720; Amara $5,900 × 75% = $4,425; Ines $1,100 × 85% = $935; Leila $4,400 × 90% = $3,960 [3]; total $10,040 [1] [4] (b) Reduction from list price at the time of sale [1]; only net invoice value recorded [1] [2]

items.stem: On 1 October Coral Bay Foods had a bank balance of $2,740. During October: (i) Grace settled a debt of $5,440 by bank transfer, less 2% cash discount (ii) Sofia paid a balance of $2,040 less 2% cash discount (iii) cash sales of $2,000 were paid directly into the bank (iv) Leila was paid the $1,100 owed, less 5% cash discount, by bank transfer (v) wages of $1,380 were paid from the bank. The bookkeeper calculated the closing bank balance as $9,740.00. Explain why this is wrong and determine the correct bank balance.
items.answer: The discounts were treated as if they were cash received or paid; discount columns are memorandum only – only the net amounts pass through the bank column. Correct bank balance: $9,645.40.
items.markingKey: Error explained: the discounts were treated as if they were cash received or paid; discount columns are memorandum only – only the net amounts pass through the bank column [1]; working: $2,740 + $9,330.40 − $2,425.00 [1]; correct bank balance: $9,645.40 [1] [3]

items.stem: Atlas Engineering keeps a petty cash book on the imprest system with a float of $500. During the week the petty cashier paid: window cleaning $6.40, stationery $63.95, travel expenses $103.05. A student said the petty cashier should be reimbursed $326.60. State the mistake made and give the correct reimbursement.
items.answer: The balance in hand was used instead of the amount spent; the imprest is restored by reimbursing what was spent. Correct reimbursement: $173.40.
items.markingKey: Error: the balance in hand was used instead of the amount spent; the imprest is restored by reimbursing what was spent [1]; correct reimbursement: $173.40 [1] [2]

The following non-routine transactions of Silk Route Textiles occurred in May: (i) office equipment costing $7,650 was bought on credit from Omar Ltd (ii) a debt of $2,200 owed by Ravi was written off as irrecoverable. The owner recorded transaction (i) as Dr Omar Ltd, Cr Office equipment. State the mistake made and give the correct journal entry.
items.answer: The debit and credit were reversed; non-current asset acquired; a non-trade payable created. Correct journal entry: Dr Office equipment $7,650, Cr Omar Ltd $7,650.
items.markingKey: Error: the debit and credit were reversed; non-current asset acquired; a non-trade payable created [1]; correct journal entry: Dr Office equipment $7,650, Cr Omar Ltd $7,650 [1] [2]

items.stem: Noah started keeping a full set of double-entry records for Atlas Engineering on 1 January. At that date the business had: Premises $77,000, Equipment $19,500, Motor vehicle $20,500, Inventory $8,100, Trade receivables $9,000, Bank $6,380, Trade payables $6,400, Bank loan (5 years) $12,000. A junior clerk credited capital with $140,480 in the opening journal. Explain the error and calculate the correct capital figure, showing your working.
items.answer: Total assets were used; capital is assets less liabilities, otherwise the journal does not balance. Correct capital figure: $122,080.
items.markingKey: Error explained: total assets were used; capital is assets less liabilities, otherwise the journal does not balance [1]; working: $140,480 − $18,400 [1]; correct capital figure: $122,080 [1] [3]

items.stem: The following non-routine transactions of Harbour Electrics occurred in May: (i) office equipment costing $5,600 was bought on credit from Nadia Ltd (ii) a debt of $5,700 owed by Tomás was written off as irrecoverable. Prepare the journal entries to record these transactions. Narratives are not required.
items.answer: (i) Dr Office equipment $5,600, Cr Nadia Ltd $5,600; (ii) Dr Irrecoverable debts $5,700, Cr Tomás $5,700
items.markingKey: (i) Dr Office equipment, Cr Nadia Ltd $5,600 [2]; (ii) Dr Irrecoverable debts, Cr Tomás $5,700 [2] [4]

items.stem: Aisha started keeping a full set of double-entry records for Volcano Spices on 1 January. At that date the business had: Premises $170,000, Equipment $31,000, Motor vehicle $13,500, Inventory $4,600, Trade receivables $10,800, Bank $3,010, Trade payables $3,600, Bank loan (5 years) $12,000. (a) Calculate the capital of the business. (b) On 5 January the business bought a machine costing $3,300 on credit from Apex Ltd. Prepare the journal entry. (c) Explain why Aisha should keep a written record (journal) of non-routine transactions.
items.answer: (a) $217,310 (b) Dr Machinery $3,300, Cr Apex Ltd $3,300; narrative: purchase of machine on credit. (c) It provides an audit trail and an explanation for unusual entries, reduces errors and helps prevent fraud.
items.markingKey: (a) Assets $232,910 − liabilities $15,600 [1]; capital $217,310 [1] [2] (b) Dr Machinery [1]; Cr Apex Ltd (other payable) [1] [2] (c) Audit trail/explanation [1]; control/fraud prevention [1] [2]
